# Prompt Injection Detection

Dimension covering detection methods — classifiers, canary tokens, semantic
analysis — and their false positive rates, with focus on orchestrator contexts.
See [citations.md](../citations.md) for source details.

## Classifier-Based Detection

### DeBERTa Fine-Tuned Models

ProtectAI's deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection reports near-perfect eval metrics:
99.99% accuracy, 99.97% recall, 99.98% precision [20]. However, v2 drops to
95.25% on untrained datasets [20], indicating overfitting to training
distribution.

### Meta Prompt Guard

Multi-label model (benign/injection/jailbreak). Prompt Guard 2 uses multilingual
base model in 86M and 22M parameter versions. **Critical vulnerability:**
bypassed via letter spacing and punctuation removal achieving up to 100%
evasion success.

On indirect injection specifically, PromptGuard 2 detects only 37.3% [21].
LlamaGuard and PromptGuard 2 cannot evaluate agentic/tool-based attack
scenarios due to architectural limitations [21].

### Over-Defense Problem

The NotInject benchmark (339 benign samples with trigger words) reveals
severe over-defense [20]:

| Model | Over-Defense Accuracy |
|---|---|
| PromptGuard | 0.88% |
| Deepset | 5.31% |
| Fmops | 5.60% |
| ProtectAIv2 | 56.64% |
| InjecGuard | 87.32% |
| Random guessing | 50% |

Most SOTA models perform worse than random guessing on benign inputs
containing attack-associated vocabulary [20]. InjecGuard's MOF training
strategy identifies biased tokens through individual evaluation, generating
contextually appropriate benign sentences for debiasing [20].

### Distribution Shift Problem

Standard evaluation overestimates performance by 8+ percentage points vs
Leave-One-Dataset-Out evaluation [21]. Detectors that appear >90% effective
on benchmark splits fail substantially on novel attack distributions [21].

## LLM-Based Detection

### PromptArmor

Uses off-the-shelf LLM to detect and remove injected prompts before agent
processing [16]. Both FPR and FNR below 1% on AgentDojo using GPT-4o,
GPT-4.1, or o4-mini as guardrail [16]. ASR drops to <1% after removal [16].
Recommended as standard baseline for defense evaluation [16].

### LLM-as-Judge

Google ADK's Gemini as Judge uses Gemini Flash Lite to evaluate inputs and
outputs for prompt injection threats [27].

**Meta-vulnerability:** LLM-based detection guardrails can themselves be
prompt-injected, creating a recursive defense problem.

### Known Answer Detection (KAD)

Structural vulnerability fundamentally compromises security guarantees.
DataFlip attack achieves 0% detection rate while inducing malicious behavior
with 91% success rate — without white-box access.

## Semantic Analysis

### PromptSleuth

Uses semantic task-level intent invariance with task summarization and
task-relationship graphs [16]. Achieves near-zero false negatives even under
obfuscation. May be more robust than surface pattern matching.

### Embedding-Based Detection

OpenAI text-embedding-3-small with XGBoost achieved 97.7% accuracy and
0.977 F1-score on prompt injection classification.

## Canary Tokens

Canary tokens provide bidirectional detection:
1. **Leakage detection:** Canary appears in output → data exfiltration
2. **Goal hijacking detection:** Canary absent from output → instructions
   overridden

Implementations: Rebuff (four-layer defense: heuristics, LLM, VectorDB,
canary tokens), Vigil LLM (16-char strings with YARA/Transformer/VectorDB
scanners). Both in alpha state.

## Multi-Agent Specific Detection Challenges

### Prompt Infection

Self-replicating prompt injections that spread through multi-agent systems
like a computer virus [11]. Neither LLM Tagging (appending markers to agent
responses) nor traditional defenses alone are sufficient — combination
required.

### Inter-Agent Message Inspection

Detection systems can wrap agent graphs, inspect inter-agent messages, and
log detections without modifying execution. However, default inter-agent
trust means agents accept whatever other agents produce without verification.

### Tool Output Sanitization

Output firewalls can reliably prevent essentially all injection attacks across
benchmark suites [17][18]. Tool-Output Sanitizer strips dangerous instructions
from tool outputs before reaching LLM. Across 400 evaluations spanning 55
unique attack types, guard agents achieved complete mitigation (20-30% to 0%).

## Production Detection Systems

### Azure Prompt Shields

Probabilistic classifier detecting User Prompt Attacks and Document Attacks
[25]. Spotlighting capability (Build 2025) distinguishes trusted vs untrusted
inputs [25]. Integrated with Microsoft Defender for Cloud [25].

### Google Gemini Classifiers

Prompt injection content classifier calibrated to 10% FPR on held-out benign
dataset [19]. Security thought reinforcement and suspicious URL redaction [19].
Continuously adapts to new attack patterns [19].

### Lakera Guard

Claims 98%+ detection, sub-50ms latency, <0.5% FPR, 100+ languages. Acquired
by Check Point in early 2026.

## Gaps and Limitations

- No detection method specifically designed for orchestrator-to-agent
  communication patterns
- Production FPR/FNR rates vs controlled benchmarks show significant gaps
- Detection latency in high-frequency inter-agent message scenarios unstudied
- Combining detection methods (semantic + classifier + canary) has no
  empirical comparison data
- Existing benchmarks biased toward single-agent scenarios
- Multi-modal injection detection (images, PDFs, HTML) poorly covered
- Cross-lingual detection in mixed-language multi-agent contexts untested
